questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Should be used on dry pavement.
Can help you maintain control when braking.
Should only be used if all axles have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you maintain control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes. It helps keep control of your vehicle and prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS works even if only one axle has it.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, and then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When going down a hill, how can you reduce how much you need to brake?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going down a hill. This helps your vehicle stay at a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: Improper coupling is:
questions.explanation: Drivers must couple and uncouple trailers correctly. Improper coupling and uncoupling is very dangerous.

questions.question: In bad weather, the driver of a double or triple should:

options.text: Lead the way for other drivers.
Drive on the shoulder of the road.
Drive carefully, as these vehicles easily skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully, as these vehicles easily skid.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, drive carefully with a double or triple. These vehicles are very prone to skidding, losing traction, and rolling over.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards, headlight glare affects vision, and there are more tired and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: If you need to back your trailer but cannot back straight, you should:

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back straight, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable?

options.text: Dual tires that do not touch each other.
Tires of different sizes if used only on short trips.
Retreaded tires on the front of a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual tires that do not touch each other.
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or other parts of the vehicle. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not have cuts or damage. Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: How can you avoid getting drowsy on a trip?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep beforehand.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue while driving: get seven to eight hours of sleep beforehand, schedule trips during your normal awake hours, plan to take breaks, and exercise regularly.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show that the system is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. Even if ABS is not working, you can still use your regular brakes.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Trust the posted signals to tell you when a train is coming.
Watch what other drivers do to know if a train is coming.
Not rely only on signals to know when a train is coming.
Look at nearby plants to see if they move from a train's breeze.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not rely only on signals to know when a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Always assume a train is coming when you approach a railroad crossing. Do not rely only on signals or hearing to know if a train is near.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Fatigue warning signs include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirror on the driver's side.
Only use the mirror on the passenger's side.

questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors often when backing up to watch for hazards. Use a helper to watch blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Rims with a missing lug nut are okay if there are at least four other lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is okay if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are okay for wheels on rear axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Cracked or bent lock rings are not safe. Welded wheel repairs are not safe.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: There is no trailer attached to the truck.
The vehicle is on a slight uphill slope.
The vehicle is on a slight downhill slope.

questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a truck, mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Compared to other commercial vehicles, combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Space management is important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Take the vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Slow down and downshift before entering a curve.
